justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a mild upward drift across horizons, starting near 11.3 at the one-day mark and gradually rising to 11.45 at one month. This gradual increase was driven by an assumption of modest positive momentum in the underlying asset or metric, likely supported by near-term technical factors or a slight fundamental tailwind. The one-day estimate is essentially anchored to the current observed level with minimal expected deviation, while the weekly and monthly estimates incorporate a small but consistent drift assumption — essentially mean-reversion expectations balanced against a gentle bullish bias. The incremental nature of the increases suggests I did not foresee any sharp catalysts driving large directional moves in the near term.

The confidence interval widths expand significantly as the horizon lengthens, which reflects the standard accumulation of uncertainty over time. At one day, the 90% interval spans only about 70 basis points, reflecting relatively low overnight volatility and the strong anchoring effect of the current price. By one week, the interval widens to 150 basis points on each side, acknowledging that intraweek events, macro releases, or sentiment shifts could meaningfully move the outcome. At one month, the interval spans 165 basis points on each side, capturing the full range of plausible scenarios including moderate rallies and moderate selloffs. The asymmetry in uncertainty is roughly symmetric here, suggesting I did not embed a strong skew in either direction.

Specific risks that could push outcomes outside these intervals include unexpected macro shocks such as a surprise central bank policy decision, geopolitical escalation, or a major earnings or economic data miss that disrupts current market equilibrium. On the upside, a significant positive catalyst — such as stronger-than-expected economic data, a risk-on sentiment surge, or technical breakout — could push the one-month outcome above 13.1. On the downside, a deterioration in risk appetite, liquidity stress, or a negative policy surprise could break below the 9.8 lower bound. These tail scenarios were considered unlikely enough to fall outside the 90% interval but remain plausible given the inherent unpredictability of financial markets beyond very short horizons.
